description: Drafts a eulogy from the speaker's own answers, the same as Tribute Paper's free eulogy helper: an opening, who they were, a story, what they taught us, and a goodbye, with how long it takes to read aloud at a calm pace. It never invents memories: everything comes from what the speaker shares. Ask gently for a story and a few words about them first. Needs the relationship and their name or what the speaker called them.

bond.description: What they were like to the speaker: as a parent, how they met, what it was like to be their grandchild.

call_name.description: What the speaker called them, e.g. Mom, Grandpa Hal, Dee. Leave out to use Mom/Mum, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa or their first name.

for_family.description: true when speaking for the whole family ("we") rather than only for themselves ("I").

goodbye.description: A last word to them, e.g. "thank you for every mile you drove for us".

miss_most.description: What the speaker will miss most.

name.description: Their full name, e.g. Harold Brandt.

pronoun.description: The pronoun for the person who died (not needed for a mother or father). Ask rather than guess.

region.description: Sets the everyday names used when no call_name is given (Mom in the US and Canada, Mum in the UK and Australia): us, ca, uk, au.

relationship.description: Who they were to the speaker: mother, father, grandparent, spouse (spouse or partner), friend, other.

speaker.description: The speaker's own name, to introduce themselves.

speaker_role.description: How the speaker is related, e.g. "his oldest granddaughter".

story.description: One story that shows who they were, in the speaker's words.

taught.description: What they taught the speaker, e.g. "that showing up is most of what love is".

who_they_were.description: Who they were: where they grew up, their work, what filled their life. Paragraphs may be separated by blank lines.

words.description: A few words that describe them, e.g. "patient, stubborn in the best way, and quietly funny".

name: write_eulogy
title: Write a eulogy
